topic.title: Multiplication Table
topic.description: Iteration using for loops. Understanding loop initialization, condition, and increment/decrement.

learningNotes.whatILearned: The same loop that counts can multiply — `n * i` for `i` from 1 to 10 is a whole table.
learningNotes.challenges: I did not check the number I read, so an empty answer gives me the table of zero and I would not even know it was wrong.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Check the `scanf` result, and put the loop bound in a comment: ten rows is the school timetable, not an arbitrary choice.

files.description: Create a Multiplication table for user.

misconceptions: `scanf` returns how many items it read — the value is only ever set if you check that, so a missing answer leaves the variable untouched
The multiplication happens inside the loop body every time, so `m` is recomputed rather than carried — that is fine, but it is worth a line saying it is deliberate
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**40 + 30 + 0 = 70%**

**What is solid**

It is correct and it is small. Given `7` it prints the table of seven from `7*1=7` down to `7*10=70`, every product right. It compiles clean under `-Wall -Wextra`.

**What is not**

`scanf("%d", &n)` is not checked, and the program prints a whole table for whatever `n` happened to be. There is also no comment anywhere, and there is one thing here that deserves a comment: `m = n * i` inside the loop rather than `m = n * 10` outside it. Both are right; the one inside the loop is the one a reader has to work out.

**The one thing to fix first**

Check the read, and add one line above the loop:

```c
/* Ten rows: the school timetable always has ten periods. */
```

That is the kind of comment that carries information the code does not.
